fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (18.5x on ~$4.60 NTM non-GAAP EPS as of Sep-2027, a ~5% haircut to FY3/28 consensus $4.58 rolled forward), FCF yield (5.5% on ~$4.60/sh FCF) and EV/EBITDA (16x ~$3.2B FY28 EBITDA less ~$3.6B net debt), all on 574M non-GAAP diluted shares incl. mandatory convertible preferred.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 ~$4.60 (FY3/28 consensus $4.58, range $4.08-$5.44; roll-forward adds growth but haircut ~5% for cycle/margin normalization toward 65% GM LT model) x 18.5x (mid-cycle analog multiple; MCHP 15x in 2022 late-cycle, 25x in early recovery; 10yr UST ~5.1% caps multiple)

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: Q1 FY27 FCF $498M (33.5% of sales); FY28 FCF ~$2.65B on ~$7.4B revenue (~36% margin, capex ~$100-150M) / 574M sh = ~$4.60/sh; 5.6% required FCF yield (levered, cyclical, net debt/EBITDA ~2.5x falling)

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY28 revenue ~$7.4B x ~43% adj. EBITDA margin = ~$3.2B; x16x = $51.2B EV; less net debt ~$3.6B by Sep-2027 (from $5.1B Jun-2026, ~$0.4B/qtr paydown) = $47.6B / 574M sh = ~$83

bear.story: Cycle rolls over in 2027: double-ordering/expedites unwind as lead times normalize (management already flags orders inside lead time), price increases lapse, GM falls back to ~60%, FY28 EPS ~$3.30, multiple compresses to ~15x with 10yr yields >5%; semis de-rate.

base.story: Recovery continues at slowing growth; revenue ~$7.2-7.5B in FY28, GM ~65% per LT model, NTM EPS ~$4.6, deleveraging continues, multiple ~18-19x. Data center (~$1B CY26, PCIe Gen6), aerospace/defense and industrial support growth.

bull.story: Extended multi-year upcycle (industrial + auto late recovery on top of AI data center), pricing sticks, EPS tracks high-end estimates ~$5.3+, leverage <2x enabling buybacks/dividend growth, multiple re-rates to 22-24x as yields ease; retakes 52w high ~$106 and beyond.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$55 (~-30%, ~12x consensus FY28 EPS) the market would be pricing a clear cyclical peak: bookings/book-to-bill falling below 1, guidance cut with distributor inventory rebuilding, and gross margin retreating toward 60%. That would mean the recovery thesis (sustained revenue growth plus deleveraging) failed, not just rate-driven multiple noise.

catalysts.event: Q2 FY27 results and Dec-qtr guide; first read on post-price-increase margins and booking trends
Q3 FY27 results; seasonal Dec-qtr and backlog visibility into CY27
Microchip investor/analyst day style updates, net leverage target <2.5x reached
Q4 FY27 results and FY28 outlook

key_uncertainties: Durability of the analog/MCU upcycle vs. double-ordering as lead times stretch to 4-8+ weeks
Whether gross margin holds near 65% after one-time licensing/distribution benefits fade
Leverage: ~$5.1B net debt limits capital return; no buybacks/dividend increases foreseen
Foundry/substrate/OSAT capacity constraints competing with AI demand limiting supply
Execution/strategy concerns around Hailo acquisition (small financially)
reasoning: Fundamentals are strong and improving: Jun-26 quarter sales $1.485B (+38% y/y, +13% q/q), non-GAAP EPS $0.76 beat; Sep-26 guide $1.603B mid and EPS $0.91-0.95, GM 66-67%, strongest bookings in ~4 years, broad price increases, FCF 33.5% of sales and net debt falling. Consensus FY3/27 EPS $3.65 and FY3/28 $4.58 have been revised up sharply (19-23 up revisions in 7 days). Yet the stock is ~26% below its 52w high ($105.91) at $78.69, down ~15% in 90 days, mainly on sector de-rating as the 10yr yield rose above 5.1% plus some Hailo skepticism and 'peak margin' caution from management itself (GM should not expand further; YoY rates flattered by depressed comps; customers ordering inside lead times, a classic late-cycle signal). At $78.69 the stock trades ~17x FY28 consensus on diluted shares, near a mid-cycle multiple, so valuation (P/E, FCF yield, EV/EBITDA) gives fair value ~$84, only modestly above spot; analyst mean target ~$108 is treated as optimistic evidence. I centered the 12-month distribution median at ~$83 (slight upside, price-only, dividend ~2.3% excluded) with lognormal sigma ~0.42 (below the 50% realized vol that included the violent 2025-26 recovery rally, but above a typical large-cap given beta ~1.7 and cyclicality), with a slightly fatter left tail for a cycle turn. Scenario mix 25/50/25 at $50/$85/$125 gives a mean ~$86, consistent with the ladder. Research relied on company release, call summary, Alpha Vantage estimates and news; no option data used.
